title: Formal or casual: register in emails and speech
summary: Choose between tú and usted, soften requests, write a formal email and recognise casual Spanish from Spain.
focus: Matching register: usted and formal email formulas vs colloquial Spanish from Spain
content:
## Tú or usted?

**Usted** is the polite *you*. It takes the third-person verb and the pronouns **le** and **su**. Use it with strangers, clients, older people, officials and anyone you write a formal letter to. **Tú** is for friends, family, children and, in Spain, most colleagues, often the boss too.

| tú | usted |
|---|---|
| ¿Tienes un momento? | ¿Tiene un momento? |
| Te escribo para… | Le escribo para… |
| tu correo | su correo |
| Siéntate. | Siéntese. |

When in doubt, start with **usted** and let the other person offer **tú**: *¿Nos tuteamos?* (Shall we say tú?) **Tutear** means to address someone as tú; **hablar de usted** means to use usted.

## Softening a request

A bare command (**Mándeme el informe**) sounds blunt. Spanish softens a request by stepping back into the past or into the conditional:

- **Quería pedirle** un favor. (I wanted to ask you a favour; polite, not past)
- **Quisiera** hablar con la directora. (I would like to speak to the director.)
- **¿Podría** enviarme el horario? (Could you send me the timetable?)
- **¿Le importaría** esperar un momento? (Would you mind waiting a moment?)
- **¿Sería tan amable de** firmar aquí? (Would you be so kind as to sign here?)

**¿Le importaría que** + imperfect subjunctive asks for permission: *¿Le importaría que abriera la ventana?* (Would you mind if I opened the window?)

## The formal email

| Part | Formal | Informal |
|---|---|---|
| Greeting | **Estimado señor Gil:** / **Estimada Sra. Ruiz:** | **Hola, Ana:** |
| Purpose | **Le escribo para** solicitar información. | Te escribo para contarte… |
| Attachment | **Adjunto le envío** el currículum. | Te mando las fotos. |
| Before closing | **Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.** | Escríbeme pronto. |
| Sign-off | **Atentamente,** | **Un abrazo,** / **Besos,** |

The greeting ends with a colon, not a comma; to a company with no name, write **Estimados señores:**. **Un saludo** (or **Saludos**) sits in between. It is polite but friendly, right for colleagues and most work emails. **Atentamente** is for strangers, companies and officials.

## Casual Spain, and when each fits

These words are everyday spoken Spanish in Spain. They are colloquial and friendly, never for a formal email or a client.

- **vale**: OK, fine. *—¿A las ocho? —Vale.*
- **guay**: cool, great. *¡Qué guay!*
- **tío / tía**: mate, dude, between friends (literally *uncle / aunt*).
- **¡qué va!**: no way, not at all. *—¿Estás cansada? —¡Qué va!*
- **me mola**: I love it, I'm into it. *Me mola tu chaqueta.*

Match the other person. A job application, a complaint, a first email to a stranger: **usted** and the formal formulas. Colleagues: **tú** and **Un saludo**. Friends: **tú** and as much **vale** and **guay** as you like. Mixing the two (*Estimado tío*) sounds like a joke.

quiz.prompt: You are writing to a company for the first time and know nobody's name. Which greeting fits?
quiz.explanation: A formal email to an unknown company opens with Estimados señores: and a colon. ¡Hola, chicos! and ¿Qué tal, tío? are for friends.
hints: Formal letter, nobody's name: estimado + colon.

quiz.prompt: ___ le envío mi currículum. (adjuntar, yo: I attach)
quiz.explanation: Adjunto le envío… (I attach…) is the standard formal formula: adjuntar in the yo form.
hints: The yo form of adjuntar ends in -o.

quiz.prompt: You end a formal complaint to an airline. Which closing fits?
options: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,
quiz.correct_answer: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,
quiz.explanation: A complaint to a company is formal: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta (I look forward to your reply) and Atentamente. Hugs and tío are for friends.
hints: Su respuesta, not tu: the airline gets usted.

quiz.prompt: You write to the director of a museum you have never met. Which request fits?
options: ¿Sería tan amable de enviarme el programa?
quiz.correct_answer: ¿Sería tan amable de enviarme el programa?
quiz.explanation: A stranger in a formal email gets usted and a softened request: ¿Sería tan amable de…? The other two use tú and colloquial words.
hints: Look for usted and a polite formula.

quiz.prompt: ¿Le ___ cerrar la ventana? (importar, polite: Would you mind closing the window?)
quiz.explanation: ¿Le importaría + infinitive? asks politely. It is the conditional of importar in the usted (third-person) form.

quiz.prompt: Your friend Marta says: «Tu chaqueta nueva me mola, es muy guay.» What does she mean?
options: She really likes your new jacket.
She thinks your new jacket is too big.
She wants to borrow your new jacket.
quiz.correct_answer: She really likes your new jacket.
quiz.explanation: Me mola (I love it) and guay (cool) are colloquial Spanish from Spain: she is paying you a compliment.

quiz.prompt: Somos compañeros, ¿nos ___? (tutear, nosotros: Shall we say tú to each other?)
quiz.explanation: Tutear is a regular -ar verb: nosotros tuteamos. ¿Nos tuteamos? is how Spaniards offer to drop usted.

quiz.prompt: Señora Molina, quería ___ un favor. (pedir + le: I wanted to ask you a favour)
quiz.explanation: The pronoun le (to you, usted) is attached to the infinitive: quería pedirle. The imperfect quería softens the request.
¡Qué va! (not at all) denies what was asked; vale means OK and guay means cool, which make no sense as an answer here.
hints: He is saying no, he isn't angry.

conversations.title: First day at the studio
conversations.scenario: Elena Vidal starts as a designer at a small studio in Valencia and meets her manager, Andrés Prieto.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenos días. ¿Es usted el señor Prieto? Soy Elena Vidal, la nueva diseñadora.
lines.meaning: Good morning. Are you Mr Prieto? I'm Elena Vidal, the new designer.
lines.note: A stranger and a boss: she starts with usted.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Encantado, Elena. Pero llámame Andrés, por favor: aquí nos tuteamos todos.
lines.meaning: Nice to meet you, Elena. But call me Andrés, please: we all say tú here.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, perfecto. Entonces, ¿me enseñas dónde está mi mesa?
lines.meaning: OK, great. So, will you show me where my desk is?
lines.note: Offered tú, she switches at once.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro, junto a la ventana. ¿Has traído el contrato firmado?
lines.meaning: Sure, by the window. Have you brought the signed contract?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, y ayer también te lo adjunté en un correo.
lines.meaning: Yes, and yesterday I also attached it to an email for you.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ah, es verdad. Una cosa: a los clientes, siempre de usted.
lines.meaning: Oh, that's right. One thing: clients, always usted.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Entendido. «Estimado señor», «Le escribo para…» y «Un saludo».
lines.meaning: Understood. 'Dear Sir', 'I am writing to…' and 'Kind regards'.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Exacto. Y nada de «tío» ni «guay» en los correos, ¿eh?
lines.meaning: Exactly. And no 'mate' or 'cool' in the emails, OK?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué va! Eso solo se lo digo a mis amigos.
lines.meaning: No way! I only say that to my friends.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me parece genial. Bienvenida al equipo.
lines.meaning: Sounds great to me. Welcome to the team.

listening.note: ¡Qué va! is colloquial and means not at all.

listening.text: ¿Le importaría hablar un poco más despacio?
listening.meaning: Would you mind speaking a little more slowly?

listening.text: Quería pedirle información sobre el curso de verano.
listening.meaning: I wanted to ask you for information about the summer course.
listening.note: Quería softens the request; it is not really past.

listening.text: Tío, el concierto de anoche fue muy guay.
listening.meaning: Mate, last night's concert was really cool.
listening.note: Colloquial Spanish from Spain, only with friends.

listening.text: Le escribo para reclamar el dinero de mi billete.
listening.meaning: I am writing to claim back the money for my ticket.
listening.note: New word: reclamar = to claim back.

listening.text: ¿Sería usted tan amable de firmar en la última página?
listening.meaning: Would you be so kind as to sign on the last page?

listening.text: Mi nueva jefa me pidió que la tuteara desde el primer día.
listening.meaning: My new boss asked me to call her tú from the first day.

listening.text: Quedamos a la espera de su respuesta y le enviamos un cordial saludo.
listening.meaning: We look forward to your reply and send you our warm regards.

guide.tip: Not sure which to use? Start with usted and wait: if they say «puedes tutearme», switch to tú.

bites.title: Tú or usted?
bites.rule: Usted (third-person verb, le, su) for strangers, clients, older people and formal letters; tú for friends, family and most colleagues in Spain. Wait to be offered tú.
bites.example_meaning: Excuse me, could you help me?

bites.title: Soften it
bites.rule: Wrap a request in quería, quisiera, ¿le importaría…? or ¿sería tan amable de…? The imperfect and the conditional make it sound less pushy.

bites.title: The formal email
bites.rule: Estimado/a + colon, Le escribo para…, Adjunto le envío…, Quedo a la espera de su respuesta, Atentamente. Un saludo is the friendlier, neutral close.
bites.example: Estimada señora Ruiz: le escribo para solicitar una cita.
bites.example_meaning: Dear Mrs Ruiz, I am writing to request an appointment.

bites.title: Casual Spain
bites.rule: Vale, guay, tío/tía, ¡qué va! and me mola are colloquial Spanish from Spain: great with friends, out of place with a client or in a formal email.

sorts.title: Formal or casual?
sorts.why: Formal formulas use usted and fixed phrases; vale, guay, tío, qué va and mola are casual words from Spain.

sorts.title: Tú or usted?
sorts.why: Usted takes the third-person verb and le/su; tú takes the second person and te/tu.

sorts.title: Where does it go in the email?
sorts.why: Estimado/a opens, le escribo and adjunto carry the message, Atentamente and Un saludo close.

spots.sentence: Estimado señor López: te escribo para pedir información.
spots.why: Estimado sets a formal tone: usted, so le escribo.
Le marks usted, which takes the third-person verb: importaría.

spots.sentence: Quedo a la espera de tu respuesta. Atentamente, Pablo Ruiz.
spots.why: A letter signed Atentamente uses usted: su respuesta.

spots.sentence: Adjunto te envío el informe, señor director.
spots.why: Señor director gets usted: Adjunto le envío.

spots.sentence: Perdone, ¿puedes decirme dónde está la estación?
spots.why: Perdone is usted, so keep it: ¿puede decirme…?
